head.citation-title: Mechanism of carbonation curing to enhance the water resistance of magnesium chlorohydrate cement containing electrolytic manganese slag
head.abstracts: © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.To enhance the water resistance of Magnesium oxychloride cement (MOC) and to achieve the resource utilization of Electrolytic manganese residue (EMR) and CO2, a synergistic modification strategy combining EMR incorporation with accelerated carbonation was proposed. The strengthening mechanisms were investigated through mechanical property testing and analyses by XRD, TG, MIP, and SEM. The results indicated that the incorporation of EMR altered the microstructure of MOC, inducing coarsening of 5Mg(OH)2·MgCl2·8 H2O phase (defined as the 5-phase) crystals and the formation of clustered structures. The reactive constituents of EMR promoted the generation of amorphous gels, thereby markedly enhancing the stability of the 5-phase crystal network. Meanwhile, to compensate for the insufficient improvement in water resistance achieved by the single incorporation of EMR and to maximize carbonation efficiency, carbonation curing was introduced during the acceleration stage of MOC hydration, facilitating CO2 ingress into the material's interior; subsequent carbonation reactions with the constituents produced carbonates. A gradient protective structure from the exterior to the interior was thereby constructed in MOC, consisting primarily of a dense composite layer formed by carbonates and gels. Upon water immersion, this compact composite layer effectively impeded moisture ingress, suppressed the decomposition of 5-phase and the continued hydration of MgO, and consequently maintained the integrity of the internal microstructure. This work confirmed that the combined use of EMR and carbonation curing produced a superior synergistic effect, significantly improving the mechanical performance and durability of MOC, while providing a new technical pathway for the high-value-added resource utilization of bulk EMR and the greenhouse gas CO2.

coredata.dc:description: To enhance the water resistance of Magnesium oxychloride cement (MOC) and to achieve the resource utilization of Electrolytic manganese residue (EMR) and CO2, a synergistic modification strategy combining EMR incorporation with accelerated carbonation was proposed. The strengthening mechanisms were investigated through mechanical property testing and analyses by XRD, TG, MIP, and SEM. The results indicated that the incorporation of EMR altered the microstructure of MOC, inducing coarsening of 5Mg(OH)2·MgCl2·8 H2O phase (defined as the 5-phase) crystals and the formation of clustered structures. The reactive constituents of EMR promoted the generation of amorphous gels, thereby markedly enhancing the stability of the 5-phase crystal network. Meanwhile, to compensate for the insufficient improvement in water resistance achieved by the single incorporation of EMR and to maximize carbonation efficiency, carbonation curing was introduced during the acceleration stage of MOC hydration, facilitating CO2 ingress into the material's interior; subsequent carbonation reactions with the constituents produced carbonates. A gradient protective structure from the exterior to the interior was thereby constructed in MOC, consisting primarily of a dense composite layer formed by carbonates and gels. Upon water immersion, this compact composite layer effectively impeded moisture ingress, suppressed the decomposition of 5-phase and the continued hydration of MgO, and consequently maintained the integrity of the internal microstructure. This work confirmed that the combined use of EMR and carbonation curing produced a superior synergistic effect, significantly improving the mechanical performance and durability of MOC, while providing a new technical pathway for the high-value-added resource utilization of bulk EMR and the greenhouse gas CO2.
coredata.dc:title: Mechanism of carbonation curing to enhance the water resistance of magnesium chlorohydrate cement containing electrolytic manganese slag
